description: §14.8.9 raw-egress fail-closed — a BRACKET access with a static string key denotes exactly the property the dot form denotes, so `new globalThis["Response"](...)` fires E-PROTECT-004 identically to `new globalThis.Response(...)` and to a bare `new Response(...)`. Pins the fix for a measured fail-open in the structural detector's FIRST cut: `a["b"]` parses to an INDEX node (types/ast.ts — `MemberExpr.property` is a plain string, computed access is `IndexExpr`), which the callee resolver did not resolve, so this exact file compiled at exit 0 with ZERO diagnostics and the emitted handler, executed, answered `{"id":1,"name":"ada","passwordHash":"$argon2id$SECRET"}`. The bracket forms `window["Response"]`, `globalThis["foo"]["Response"]`, `globalThis["Response"].json(...)` and `Response["json"](...)` all reach the same conclusion.
rationale: §14.8.9's closed-world precondition (SPEC.md:8519-8525) puts the SHALL on the CONSTRUCT — 'a manual `Response` / `handle()` body (§40)' — not on a spelling of it, so a detector that recognises one surface form and not another under-enforces the normative rule. A bracket with a string-literal key is STATICALLY RESOLVABLE: the key's value is on the `lit` node the parser already built, so reading it is the tree's own answer, not a re-scan of source text (invariant 55). The residual is the genuinely dynamic key (`let k = "Response"; globalThis[k]`), whose value is not in the tree — that needs the name resolver / constant propagation, and it is stated as a bound in `detectProtectedRawEgress` rather than claimed closed. provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S352 (dpa-029 Q1).
